text.p: Italian debt markets came under another day of pressure as the lira lost ground on the mark amid continuing concerns about prospects for European monetary union.
The lira lost its footing and flopped headlong to 1,007.25 per mark, its weakest point against the mark since mid-November.
It dragged the debt markets with it, although dealers said the move down was on light volumes.

Luca Jellinek, bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets, said expectations G7 interest rates were -- long term -- now on the way up has pulled the rug from under bond market sentiment while doubt EMU would start in 1999 was doing the rest.

The June LIFFE Btp future was 29 basis points down at 124.06 having touched 123.60 following comments from Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said delay in EMU was the only option if Germany did not meet all the Maastricht criteria.
The November 2006 Btp was one basis point down at 99.80 and yielding 7.92 percent with a spread over the benchmark Bund of 201. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 27 bps lower at 104.78.
"The currency was under pressure and there was a big sell off on Btps but on light volumes," one broker in London said.
Jellinek said trading seemed mostly intraday but he added: "The bear is fairly satisfied this going to be a bear market."
Jellinek said the outlook for Btps was bearish with the next significant support level at 122.72. He expected to see the market sliding gradually in the context of a general bond market downtrend.

As far as Italian fundamentals are concerned, the first set of preliminary March inflation data arrive on Thursday with analysts expecting a year on year rate of 2.3 percent against 2.4 percent in February. Otherwise the market continues to watch for any fresh information on the proposed Italian mini-budget.
